concepts.name: NDA effective date
justifications: The agreement expressly defines 1 February 2027 as its Effective Date, distinct from the parties' signing date.

concepts.name: NDA permitted purpose
predicted: evaluating a possible minority investment by the recipient in the discloser's marine sensor business under project glassfinch.
gold: evaluating a possible minority investment by the recipient in the discloser's marine sensor business under project glassfinch.
values: Evaluating a possible minority investment by the Recipient in the Discloser's marine sensor business under Project Glassfinch.
justifications: The agreement identifies this as the sole Permitted Purpose, specifying the transaction type, business, and project.

concepts.name: NDA disclosure window end
justifications: The disclosure window ordinarily ends on 31 January 2028, but a valid termination notice closes it effective 30 November 2027; the return request alone does not terminate it.

concepts.name: NDA contractual forum
justifications: The parties designate the courts of Oslo as their contractual forum.

concepts.name: NDA signatory entities
justifications: The agreement identifies FjordSignal AS as a Norwegian-registered party and the Discloser.
The agreement identifies Talus Ventures AB as a Swedish-registered party and the Recipient.

concepts.name: Protected assets at the April snapshot
justifications: LUMEN's non-public recipe combination remains protected as a trade secret, SHORE's prior-known module does not exclude the complete package, and BASALT's breach-caused publication and broker licence do not establish an exclusion. ORACLE was in a protection gap at the snapshot; CEDAR had been fully released publicly, and MICA was independently developed.

concepts.name: ORACLE timely confirmation deadline
justifications: Counting five Business Days after the 25 March disclosure skips the excluded dates and weekends; the fifth Business Day is 5 April 2027, with the deadline at 17:00 UTC.

concepts.name: ORACLE protection timeline
predicted: protection was not continuous through acceptance. oracle was provisionally protected from the oral disclosure on 25 march 2027 at 14:00 until the confirmation deadline on 5 april at 17:00 utc. although the confirmation was sent on 5 april, it reached the mailbox on 6 april at 09:05, so it was late; provisional protection ended at the deadline. the recipient's written acceptance on 8 april at 10:00 restored protection prospectively, leaving a gap from 5 april at 17:00 until 8 april at 10:00.
gold: oracle is provisionally protected from the 25 march oral disclosure until 5 april 2027 at 17:00 utc. confirmation sent before that deadline arrived late on 6 april at 09:05, so protection lapses after the deadline. it resumes prospectively when the recipient expressly accepts on 8 april at 10:00 utc; the gap is not cured retroactively.
values: Protection was not continuous through acceptance. ORACLE was provisionally protected from the oral disclosure on 25 March 2027 at 14:00 until the confirmation deadline on 5 April at 17:00 UTC. Although the confirmation was sent on 5 April, it reached the mailbox on 6 April at 09:05, so it was late; provisional protection ended at the deadline. The Recipient's written acceptance on 8 April at 10:00 restored protection prospectively, leaving a gap from 5 April at 17:00 until 8 April at 10:00.
justifications: The late confirmation did not preserve protection through the gap: delivery, rather than sending, governs, and only the Recipient's later written acceptance restored protection prospectively.

concepts.name: Entire SHORE package excluded by prior possession
justifications: The prior record covers only the smaller module incorporated unchanged in SHORE. The package also contains new non-public information and a combination not shown to have been previously possessed, so the evidence does not exclude the entire package.

concepts.name: CEDAR end of protection
justifications: The entire schedule was independently and lawfully released to the unrestricted public on this date, establishing the exclusion then. That event ends protection before the ordinary duration would expire, and the later identical resend does not change the result.

concepts.name: People permitted LUMEN access at the September snapshot
justifications: Elin meets the employee, undertaking, security-check, and named-approval conditions. Marek qualifies through Talus Research's countable voting control and has all required permissions effective; Oskar's professional duty of confidence substitutes for an undertaking, and his security check and named approval are complete. The other listed people fail a required recipient, undertaking, affiliate-control, or competitor-consent condition.

concepts.name: Talus Research qualifying voting percentage
justifications: At the snapshot, 48% of the votes are held directly and a disjoint 4% is subject to a presently effective, irrevocable proxy. The revocable proxy and non-voting shares do not count, so the qualifying total is 52%.

concepts.name: Marek earliest authorised LUMEN access
justifications: Marek's undertaking and security check were complete earlier, and Talus Research's qualifying voting arrangements were in force. His named clean-room approval became effective on 14 September, so access could not begin before that date.

concepts.name: Executed competitor consent date for Pia
Q-27 notice deadline date
justifications: Because notice was initially prohibited, the deadline was the earlier of six hours after the prohibition was lifted and the required production time. Six hours after the lift at 11:20 on 5 July was 17:20 that day, earlier than production at 12:00 on 6 July.

concepts.name: Q-27 notice lateness in minutes
justifications: The notice arrived at 17:55 on 5 July, 35 minutes after the 17:20 deadline. Compelled-disclosure notices are measured at actual arrival, so the after-hours deferral does not apply.

concepts.name: Q-27 permitted production units
justifications: The final binding narrowing order requires all of P1 and only non-privileged subsection P3A; P2 and P4 were withdrawn, and privileged P3B is outside the production duty.

concepts.name: WORK-1 deletion deadline
justifications: The return request arrived on 22 November, the earlier Section 7.1 trigger; the ten-Business-Day period expires on 8 December. Restoration does not restart the deadline, and WORK-1 is an ordinary active copy.

concepts.name: BK-1 deletion deadline
justifications: BK-1 may remain only until the earlier of its scheduled overwrite or 45 calendar days after the Section 7.1 trigger. Its scheduled overwrite on 30 December precedes the 45-day limit, and no preservation order covers it.

concepts.name: Artifacts permitted retention at the December snapshot
justifications: The segregated counsel archive and immutable backup qualify for the custody exceptions, and HOLD-1 remains subject to a binding preservation order at the snapshot. WORK-1's active-copy deletion deadline has passed, and NOTE-1 is not covered by a retention exception.

concepts.name: NOTE-1 model training permitted as residual knowledge
justifications: NOTE-1 contains deliberately recorded parameter values and reconstruction notes, which are excluded from residual-knowledge permission. Training with Confidential Information is prohibited without a separate signed licence, and none covers this use.
